answer: Because the fable audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm therefore spreads across origins and burns for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the beacon quota and the forge admission check. Admission is capped at 6 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
